title: Choose Life!
description: This article addresses depression and suicidal thoughts, providing statistics and explaining their connection. It discusses the role of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) in navigating such crises, emphasizes the importance of seeking professional help, and highlights the availability of free psychological support. The text is supportive, reminding readers of the value of life and the importance of holding onto hope.

texts: Since we are exploring the labyrinths of negative thinking and depression, we must pause at the most difficult yet vital topic — suicidal thoughts.

We sincerely hope you have never experienced this abyss. But if death has ever felt like the only way out of the darkness — whether in the past or right now — we are here to support you, and we want to talk about it with care and honesty.
According to the World Health Organization, a vast number of people face this tragedy every year. And those are only the cases we know about.

The statistics are harsh: throughout human history, suicide losses have been comparable to war casualties. These numbers are painful, but they scream one thing: the scale of this pain is colossal, and so many people are going through the same struggle.
<important>Depression plays a key role here. A huge portion of these tragedies occurs alongside depressive disorders, when the risk of being unable to endure the pain increases manifold.</important>
We aren’t telling you this to frighten you. We want to break the silence. Many people hide their pain out of shame, thinking, “I’m the only one,” even though help is truly within reach.
Thoughts of not wanting to live are not a sign of weakness, being “broken,” or losing. There is no shame in them.

People reach this edge for many different reasons, but they are often united by one thing: unbearable, suffocating emotional pain. When it feels endless, death can start to seem like the only way to breathe.

Sometimes it is a cry for relief from suffering, or a heavy, distorted desire to “stop being a burden” to loved ones. Please understand: this is despair speaking, not a true assessment of how valuable and needed you are.

Psychology confirms that the main catalyst is an absolute sense of hopelessness. When depression distorts perception, the world narrows down to a single black dot, and the future feels completely shut tight.
But the most important thing to realize is this: hopelessness and despair are symptoms of your condition, not objective reality.
The decision to give up is often built on the illusion that “it will never get better.” But is that a fact? Does depression have any real evidence that this darkness is permanent?
When everything hurts inside, it is impossible to imagine a brighter tomorrow. In moments like these, advice like “just think positive” can feel invalidating and only worsens the sense of guilt.
You are not to blame for anything. It can feel as if your mind is stuck in thick mud. This pain is absolutely real, and there is no switch to simply “turn off” your feelings at the click of a button.

But try, just for a moment, to entertain one thought: this impenetrable darkness is merely a pair of dark, distorted glasses that depression has placed on you. They ruthlessly distort your view of the world.
Hold onto that thought like a lifeline: any lenses can be cleaned. The darkness will dissipate, and you are so much more than your current struggles.
And these aren’t just comforting words. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a proven, effective method used worldwide to help people navigate through crises safely.

<important>Global research confirms: CBT doesn’t just provide temporary relief; it significantly reduces the risk of suicidal thoughts returning and provides a clear action plan for when it feels like there is no way out.</important>
Yes, this path will require strength. But CBT puts real, practical tools in your hands, helping ensure that your efforts lead to meaningful change.
In a separate section, we will go into detail on how to work through depression using CBT, including how to manage suicidal thoughts.
We aim to spark a desire to live within you, but only a professional can truly guide you out of the darkness.

If you feel like you are standing on the edge — please, do not wait. Reach out to a doctor, a psychotherapist, or a crisis hotline right now (if there is an immediate threat, call emergency services immediately).
<q author="Thomas Fuller">The darkest hour is just before the dawn.</q>
Even if you cannot afford private sessions, many countries and cities have centers that offer anonymous, free, and immediate help. Taking the first step means choosing life.
We understand how terrifying and difficult it is to speak up about this. But a professional is there to help you weather this storm and teach you how to find your footing again.
We believe that with support, you can step by step rebuild a warm, kind, and strong relationship with yourself and the world.
Life can be harsh, and difficult periods happen to many. But this world is vast and beautiful, and your life is of absolute value. Please, remember this: the world is worth living in!
